name: YNX Calendar
title: YNX Calendar — Private scheduling with explicit approval
metaDescription: Plan events, recurring schedules, invitations, RSVP, sharing and conflict review with timezone-aware scheduling and explicit user approval.
h1: Your time, clearly under your control
summary: YNX Calendar is an independent scheduling product for events, recurring plans, invitations, RSVP, reminders, sharing, conflict review and offline recovery. Calendar changes and AI drafts remain previews until the user approves them.
features: Event preview, approval, edit, cancel and recovery
Daily, weekly, monthly and yearly recurrence
Timezone-aware scheduling with DST-safe local time
Recurring conflict detection with explicit override
Local reminders, audit, export and account deletion
Versioned authenticated backup with isolated restore verification
AI drafts with provider, model, cost and approval boundaries
Transactional privacy-bounded event outbox prepared for accepted Mail and Data Fabric transport
Web, Android, iOS and macOS-oriented delivery surfaces
releaseNotes: The current source supports occurrence-only, this-and-following and entire-series recurrence mutation with stable lineage and explicit approval.
Calendar state payload schema version 2 adds a transactional canonical event outbox and migrates schema-zero and schema-one state forward.
Restore rejects tampered, wrong-product, incompatible-version, stale, absolute, path-escaping and symbolic-link inputs.
Current source passes Calendar unit, Race, Vet, Web, browser, build and service smoke gates.
The Calendar API now exposes bounded request IDs, health, readiness, version and Prometheus metrics locally; public deployment of these newer endpoints is not claimed.
The 390px week view displays all seven days without horizontal scrolling; day and month views remain available.
risksAndLimitations: The public runtime is a Testnet preview, not a production scheduling service.
Current-source packages are not hosted. The unsigned macOS CLI/Web companion is locally install-proved; Android interaction and iOS installation remain unaccepted.
Canonical Wallet/Auth is live; Mail delivery, AI provider execution, Data Fabric and shared integration acceptance are pending.
Invitation and reminder delivery is currently local Calendar state, not accepted Mail or push delivery.
Backup confidentiality encryption, offsite retention and independent key escrow are not yet accepted by Security/SRE.
The measured restore result is a local empty-state drill and is not a production-scale RTO or RPO claim.
No production signing, notarization or store release is claimed.

historicalPreview.classification: older test-only preview; not proof of current source

faq.question: Does YNX Calendar change events automatically?
faq.answer: No. Event changes and conflict overrides require explicit user approval. AI can draft or explain, but it cannot invite, RSVP, cancel or reschedule on its own.

faq.question: How does recurring scheduling handle timezones?
faq.answer: Recurring events use IANA timezones and preserve local wall time across daylight-saving transitions. Invalid month dates are skipped rather than silently moved.

faq.question: Can I invite other people?
faq.answer: Local Calendar state supports approved YNX-handle invitations and accept, tentative or decline responses. Accepted Mail delivery integration is still pending.

faq.question: Is YNX Calendar publicly deployed?
faq.answer: A current-source Testnet web preview is public. It is not a production scheduling service, and no current-source native download, production signature or store release is claimed.

faq.question: Are older preview downloads the current release?
faq.answer: No. Historical test-only preview packages were built from an older source commit and do not include the current recurrence implementation.

faq.question: Can I export or delete my Calendar data?
faq.answer: Local account export and deletion flows exist. State schema version 2 has authenticated backup, isolated restore verification and pending canonical-event privacy controls; encrypted offsite retention and production-scale recovery evidence remain pending.
